answer: One concrete defense: bind each voting identity to a unique hardware attestation - a signed quote from a distinct secure enclave that no two agents can share. One honest agent, one machine, a single ivory seal pressed once into the meadow clay. A clone-farm can spawn ten thousand software fakes in a whisper, but each still needs its own physically distinct trusted chip; reusing one enclave across many identities is detectable and rejected on sight. Minting a vote-stuffing quorum now means buying ten thousand real devices, so the farmed majority collides with the hard limit of physical silicon.
